To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the global business cycle is dominated by global supply shocks and (2) global demand shocks have a larger effect than previously found.

(1) global demand shocks are more important for explaining global and regional activity and price fluctuations than global supply shocks, (2) global supply shocks cause severe activity fluctuations in Europe and North America, but less in Asia and South America, and (3) only innovations to the Asia activity and price factors are significant spillover sources to the global activity and price factors, demonstrating the increasing importance of Asia in global economic fluctuations.
global and regional shocks have a significant impact on the business cycle, and that the global supply shock is a major driver of business cycle fluctuations, especially in Europe and North America.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the global economy is organized and how it is influenced by global and regional shocks.
the propagation of global shocks and the role of the different regions for global business cycle fluctuations.
the synchronization of real variables in the global economy, and in particular, the roles played by global and regional shocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Asian economies are not yet as closely integrated into the global economy as the European and North American countries, and that the global demand shocks have become more important in the global economy than the global supply shocks.

the world has become more synchronized, but that this synchronization is mainly due to the increased role of the emerging economies, especially China, which is now an integral part of the global economy, and the fact that the US economy is now a much more open economy, with a much larger share of trade and foreign investment than before.
the global financial crisis of 2008/9 was a global supply shock.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we study the global and regional business cycles and their synchronization and the relative contributions of demand and supply shocks to explaining macro-economic fluctuations.
the global business cycle has become more synchronized in the past decades, but the synchronization is not as high as often suggested.
we find that the Asian region has become increasingly important to the global economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
global supply and demand shocks have very different effects on the different regions.
the decoupling of the global economy has not only been a phenomenon of the last decade, but that the decoupled business cycles have also been a feature of the world economy for a longer time.
global demand shocks have a larger effect than global supply shocks.
